title: Chapter 31 — The Name That Was Crossed Out

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 31

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Name That Was Crossed Out
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall behind the kneeling statue began to open without a sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: White limestone parted along a seam that had not existed a breath earlier. Cold air moved out of the darkness beyond, carrying the same faint scent of ozone and old copper that clung to the ledger chamber. The statue rose and stepped aside with the same unthinking precision it had shown since the corridor first closed behind them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They entered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The chamber beyond was larger than the name corridor and colder. The walls here were still white limestone, still covered in rows of personal names, but the cuts were deeper and the crossed-out lines more frequent. Condensation wept down the stone in thin sheets that smelled of a forge just before the metal comes out of the fire, though there was no heat—only cold that behaved as if it remembered being hot.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The grain beneath the moisture slid like sand in an hourglass. Looking away and looking back had become its own kind of danger.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek found himself staring at a jagged, freshly etched stroke that looked like a scar cut into the stone.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: BAH-lahg,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said. His voice sounded strangely distant even to himself.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It's your name. It's crossed out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stepped forward. His face had gone pale. He was not a man who scared easily—Zeek had seen him stand his ground against things with teeth and things with blades and things that were neither—but there was a particular kind of fear that came from being told your own name was written somewhere you could not see it, and that fear had him now.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: You're losing your mind, Zeek,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said, though there was no real conviction behind it.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: There's nothing there but a blur.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He leaned closer anyway.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stone under Zeek's gaze continued to rearrange itself. The crossed-out name that had looked like BAH-lahg's a moment earlier was already softening into something else. A different set of characters rose, then blurred, then settled into a shape Ninsun recognized before anyone else did.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She went still.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That one is mine.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo looked from one of them to the other, then at the wall, calculating even without the desire that had once made calculation feel like survival.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: Both of you can't be right.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We can if the ledger is rewriting itself as we watch,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun said. Her voice had gone thin.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Or if it is showing each of us the account it intends to close next.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The scraping resumed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Scrape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Scrape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Pause.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It came from everywhere at once—sometimes from the wall ahead, sometimes from beneath the floor, once, impossibly, from somewhere directly behind Zeek's eyes, as though the sound had found a way to skip the ears and carve straight into the meat of his skull. He had stopped trying to locate it. Guessing implied the room followed rules the room had already refused.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg backed away from the wall.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't like this place.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: You said that about the last one,
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo answered, but the dryness in her voice was thinner than before.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek kept watching the stone. A new name rose under the condensation, held long enough for him to read it, then began to close over itself the way skin closes over a wound. He knew the name. A merchant who sold grain near the Street of Scribes. A man who had once shorted him three measures and laughed when Zeek noticed. An ordinary man under an ordinary sky who, at that very moment, was almost certainly still haggling over prices.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It looked less like killing than removing the evidence that anyone had ever been known.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun's stylus hovered over parchment that no longer accepted ink the way it once had.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: It's testing which threads it can pull without the fabric noticing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg shook his head hard, as if the motion itself might dislodge something that had begun to settle.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: I don't know what you're talking about. Where is the rest of the crew?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The question landed harder than any shout could have, because it was not rhetorical. He meant it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ninsun looked toward the empty space beside them. Recognition broke across her face, incomplete and unstable.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: KOO-rash,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she whispered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek followed her gaze. He could almost retrieve the shape—someone younger, ambitious, always calculating his share before the work was finished. The memory arrived in fragments: a voice complaining about the stairs, an extra waterskin that no one had claimed since the ridge, five bedrolls marked in the sand when only four people seemed present. The details had been there the entire time. They had simply stopped belonging to anyone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-HEH-doo frowned at the empty space.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: I remember a knife. Not the hand that carried it.
lines.note: Post-vision (Ch.29+): same voice, flattened affect. Even pitch, slower, no reach.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg stared at them as though they had begun speaking a language he had never learned.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Who?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The City had not merely been changing the walls around them.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It had been cutting pieces directly out of their heads.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Not only names.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The threads connecting those names to the living.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: One relationship at a time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek stared at the place where the merchant's name had been. The stone had already smoothed over the letters. His breathing had gone shallow. He looked at Ninsun, who was watching his face with a terrible, focused intensity, as though trying to memorize it before it could be taken from her too.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Zeek,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she whispered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Tell me your name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His mouth opened.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Nothing came out.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The answer was there—he knew, with a certainty that had nothing to do with actually possessing it, that it was there, somewhere behind a wall, behind a door, behind something that had already been carved away and smoothed over before he had even noticed the cutting. He looked down at his palm. The wedge-shaped lines beneath the skin crawled like insects disturbed from beneath a stone.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For one terrible, suspended second he could not remember whether Zee-keer Ash-SHOOR was his name at all, or simply a name he had been told to answer to.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wall behind him began to scrape again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This time the chisel was not working on someone else's name.
